ElevationLease.description:
One decided elevation: the request (what was asked and why) plus the
authority's decision. `approved: false` records a DENIAL — evidence
that the authority saw and refused the ask. Only `approved` leases
with no revocation and an unexpired window license anything.

approved.description:
False records an explicit denial; the remaining fields still
journal who decided and when.

expires_at.description:
For an approval: the hard window edge (automatic revocation —
every check compares against the reading clock, so an expired
lease licenses nothing without any sweeper running). For a
denial: equals `decided_at`.

id.description: The deciding command's id: the lease's durable identity.

reason.description:
Why the worker needs this, supplied with the request and recorded
with the decision. Never a secret or an unbounded path.

revoked_at.description:
Sticky manual revocation: once set, the lease is dead regardless
of its window.

task_id.description:
The elevated dispatch and its task — every active lease is
attributable to exactly one dispatch.

oneOf.description:
The published Compatibility Dossier this Host holds for the runtime this
binding's primary candidate declares, served whole and named by the run
inside it that certifies that runtime. The document is served only after
it has been held against the declaration the Host actually has: a record
for another pack, a shape this crate does not speak, a rule the record
does not show as held, a matrix that is not the suite's, a run over no
work, a version the pack published no run for, or a run of another
adapter build is refused by name rather than served.

The caller's Project registry: every registered Project it may read.
The Host answers with the records the authenticated caller is
authorized for, so the list is scoped by the same per-Project
authorization `GetProject` applies to one record rather than by the
connection. The list names no path: a Project's identity is its stable
`ProjectId`.

One Project's canonical records — the Project, its Roots, its Roles and
its Tasks — with the cursor of the Project's own journal at the moment
of the read: the records include the effect of every event with
`sequence <= cursor` and of no later event, so a client bootstraps from
one read instead of replaying the log.

max_cpu_millicores.description:
The CPU the candidate's dispatch needs, in millicores. Absent means the
candidate declares no CPU demand and the readiness report asks the Host
for none: concurrency is not a CPU reservation.

host_paths.description: An observed placement, not identity or filesystem authorization.

requested.description: Explicit Lead/user assignment; honored before classification.

oneOf.description: This task cannot start until the target completes.
This task consumes a versioned contract produced by the target.
This task blocks the target (stored on the blocking task).
This task independently reviews the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task independently verifies the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task supersedes the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task conflicts with the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task follows up on the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.

Timestamp.description: UTC milliseconds from Unix epoch, assigned by the authority, not a worker clock.

WorkEdit.description: Canonical completion is deliberately absent from client operations.

command_id.description: The durable idempotency key, scoped by the Host to authenticated intent.

correlation_id.description: A retry may use a new correlation ID; it must retain its command ID.

BindingSurfaces.description:
The surfaces a binding demands, as the runtime the Host observed declares
them, read one step before the contract projection: a binding and the
Host's observation of a runtime, with no Task Contract compiled yet and no
dispatch identity to name.

The demand is the binding's own — the enforcement minimums its policy
declares, the capabilities its policy requires and the tools and skills it
names, which the dispatch boundary requires the same way. Nothing a runtime
advertises becomes a requirement here either, and the twelve surfaces are
the same twelve the contract projection covers.

adapter.description:
The runtime the demand was read onto: the descriptor's own identity, so a
carriage names the exact adapter, installation, profile, model, host and
versions it was read from.

binding.description: The binding whose demand was read.

surfaces.description: Every surface in [`ContractSurface::ALL`], in that order.

oneOf.description: A blocking dependency target is not Completed.
The owning Change Stream is not Active (collided, integrated...).
Another task holds a lease on this task's stream — serialized by policy.

CandidateObservation.description:
What this Host holds for one candidate the binding names. The three cases are
the three facts, never collapsed: an operator who declared nothing, an
observation this Host cannot attribute to itself, and this Host's own
observation of the runtime it would activate.

oneOf.description: The operator declared no runtime for this candidate's profile.

A runtime was observed for this candidate's profile, but not by this
Host's own pulse. An observation this Host cannot attribute to itself is
not a statement about the runtime it would activate.

This Host's observation of the runtime it declared for this profile, read
onto the binding's demand: the carriage names, per surface, what the
declaration carries for every control the binding declares a minimum for
and every carrier its policy or named resources require.

CandidateSurfaces.description:
One candidate the binding may be staffed with, and what this Host holds for
it. The primary is first and the fallbacks follow in the binding's own order.
The report publishes this and selects nothing: whether a fallback may be used
is the binding's own consent policy, and the choice is activation's.

CapabilityRead.description:
One capability the module places on a surface, read beside what the
adapter's own projections carry for it. This is the capability matrix, and it
is wire data: a published dossier carries these rows as they were read.

capability.description: The carrier this row is about.

carried.description:
Whether every place that demands it reports it carried as declared. A
capability no dispatch demands is read as carried in the sense its
declaration states: nothing contradicts it.

declared.description:
The descriptor's own declaration, in the projection's own vocabulary, so
both readers agree on what four facts are four. A capability the
descriptor never mentions is `Absent` rather than assumed.

demanded.description: Whether any dispatch the suite ran demands this capability.

CarrierDelivery.description:
What the descriptor holds for one capability the contract demands on a
surface. The three refusals stay distinct: a runtime that declares a
capability unsupported, one that has not established it, and one that never
mentioned it are three different facts, and none of them is support.

oneOf.description: The descriptor declares the capability supported.
The descriptor declares it unsupported.
The descriptor has not established it.
The descriptor does not mention it.

CompatibilityDossier.description: A pack's published record of what it was run against.

adapter.description:
The pack this dossier is: its adapter, and the harness driver it drives
when it drives an external one.

runs.description:
One entry per upstream version and platform the pack was run against, in
the order the pack published them.

schema_version.description: The dossier shape this document speaks.

ConformanceRun.description: One conformance run, as a pack publishes it.

adapter.description:
The adapter this run was of, and the harness driver it drives when it
drives an external one.

capabilities.description: The suite's capability matrix, as that run read it.

controls.description: The suite's enforcement matrix, as that run read it.

dispatches.description: What each dispatch in the run published.

rules.description: One outcome per rule the suite ran, in the suite's own order.

tier.description: The tier the runtime declared, which implies nothing by itself.

upstream_version.description:
The upstream product version, the adapter's own version and the platform,
each read from the descriptor the run was made over — never supplied by
the pack, which is the whole point: a version nobody ran against cannot
appear here.

withheld.description:
The surfaces that run's projections carried nothing for, in this crate's
own order.

ContractSurface.description:
A place a Workforce Runtime Contract fact must be carried for the runtime to
act under it. The names describe the *place*, not a harness: an adapter maps
its own protocol file, brief, sandbox or registration onto these, and a
runtime that has no place for one has to say so rather than appear to have it.

oneOf.description: The stable Workforce Protocol the dispatch was compiled under.
The routed Role's operating contract.
The Task Contract and the context handed to the worker with it.
The skills the binding requires the worker to hold.
The tools and MCP registrations the binding requires, and nothing else.

Native permissions and sandboxing: the filesystem, process and network
confinement the contract claims over this execution.
Hooks and event delivery the runtime can be driven through.
Plugins and extensions the runtime loads.

The environment the worker runs in: its own profile's home and
configuration rather than the Host's ambient ones.

References to secrets the execution is authorized to use. The projection
names the references; no secret value enters it.

Verification and exit signals the worker produces. Carries signals only:
the contract's `CompletionAuthority` claim is what keeps a worker's own
report from being completion.

Cleanup and teardown after the execution, under the contract's
`Cancellation` claim.

ControlRead.description:
One control the module places on a surface, with what the descriptor
declares and what the adapter's projections made of it. This is the
enforcement matrix, and it is wire data for the same reason.

control.description: The claim this row is about.

declared.description:
The strength the descriptor declares, or `None` when it does not list
the control at all.

demanded.description: Whether any dispatch the suite ran claims this control on its surface.

mechanism.description: The mechanism the descriptor names, or `None` when it lists no control.

realized.description:
Whether every place that demands it reports it carried — delivered or
degraded, since a degradation is realized. A control no dispatch demands
is read as realized in the sense its declaration states: nothing
contradicts it.

surface.description: The one surface this module places the control on.

lease_dispatch_id.description: The lease binding (dispatch + fencing token) when a held lease exists.

provider_connection.description:
The provider identities the task's dispatch profile names. Present
whenever a profile resolved, even when its registration was refused.

role_id.description: The routed Role, present only when routing resolved.

worktree_id.description: The stream's reserved worktree identity and branch.

DispatchRead.description:
What one dispatch's projection published. Wire data for the same reason: a
dossier says which abstract work each of its runs was read over, so a reader
can tell a run over a bare task from a run over a staffed one.

surfaces.description: How many surfaces the projection names.

withheld.description: The surfaces the projection carries nothing for, in the module's order.

DossierHolding.description:
The published record a Host holds, and the run in it that certifies the
runtime this Host declares. The record is the pack's own document, served
whole; the pair is the Host's answer to which of its runs was held.

platform.description: The platform of the run this Host held.

upstream_version.description: The upstream version of the run this Host held.

ElevationLease.description:
One decided elevation: the request (what was asked and why) plus the
authority's decision. `approved: false` records a DENIAL — evidence
that the authority saw and refused the ask. Only `approved` leases
with no revocation and an unexpired window license anything.

approved.description:
False records an explicit denial; the remaining fields still
journal who decided and when.

expires_at.description:
For an approval: the hard window edge (automatic revocation —
every check compares against the reading clock, so an expired
lease licenses nothing without any sweeper running). For a
denial: equals `decided_at`.

id.description: The deciding command's id: the lease's durable identity.

reason.description:
Why the worker needs this, supplied with the request and recorded
with the decision. Never a secret or an unbounded path.

revoked_at.description:
Sticky manual revocation: once set, the lease is dead regardless
of its window.

task_id.description:
The elevated dispatch and its task — every active lease is
attributable to exactly one dispatch.

ElevationRequest.description:
A worker's ask for one permission beyond its binding. Observation
only: filing this never licenses anything. Only a later
[`ElevationLease`] decided by the owner can.

id.description: The requesting command's id: the ask's durable identity.

reason.description: Why the worker needs this. Never a secret or an unbounded path.

EventPayload.description: Durable events are server output. There is no wire command to append one.

oneOf.description:
Every composition step succeeded; the referenced ids identify the
durable artifacts a Start transition may consume.
One or more composition steps refused, with the recorded reasons.

The provider registration the primary candidate's profile names, judged
by the same registry validation the execution boundary uses.

Whether this Host can honour the limits the candidate declares at all:
the same decision activation makes before it runs anything
(`ResourceLimits::process_bound`). A declared limit the Host has no
kernel bound for is not a capacity question — the Host may well have
the capacity and still refuse the run — so it is reported here, with the
reason the run will refuse on, instead of being left to contradict a
satisfied capacity check.

Whether the observed runtime carries, on the surfaces the projection
places them, the facts this binding demands: the enforcement minimums its
policy declares, the capabilities that policy requires, and the tools and
skills the binding names — which the dispatch boundary requires the same
way, so a report that omitted them would contradict the decision
activation makes. The refusal names the withheld surfaces, so an operator
reads *where* the runtime carries nothing rather than only that
something is missing.

Whether the candidate's own lane can execute at all given the access its
snapshot grants. The external lane's dispatch IS a Host-launched
sandboxed process, and it can never acquire the process grant later
(capability elevation refuses an `EXTERNAL_HARNESS` dispatch), so a
candidate for that lane which does not grant `ExecuteProcess` is
`rejected` here instead of being reported ready and then refused by the
sandbox at the transport build.

limit_refusal.description:
Present exactly on the enforceable-limits prerequisite, and only when a
declared limit cannot be bound: the declared limit in the one vocabulary
activation refuses on, so the report names the reason the run will give
rather than leaving the operator to discover it by starting.

provider_refusal.description:
Present exactly on the provider prerequisite, and only when the registry
refused: the refusal's own name, so the report says why a dispatch would
not run rather than merely that it would not.

withheld_surfaces.description:
Present exactly on the runtime-surfaces prerequisite, and only when the
observed runtime carries nothing for a surface the binding demands: the
surfaces themselves, in their declared order, so the refusal names the
places rather than a count.

PreventiveDelivery.description: What the descriptor holds for one control the contract claims over a surface.

oneOf.description: The runtime's own declared control realizes the contract's claim.

The runtime carries the control, but weaker than the contract claims —
an observed or emulated mechanism where the contract claims prevention.
Both strengths are retained: the degradation is a fact routing,
permissions, UI and certification read, not a delivery to assume.
The descriptor does not list this control at all. Nothing carries it.

ProjectSnapshot.description:
A Project read as one point in its journal: the canonical records the
Project's own reads answer, with the cursor of the Project's journal at the
moment of the read. The records include the effect of every event with
`sequence <= cursor` and of no later event, so a client may resume from
`cursor` rather than replaying the log. A snapshot that cannot fit the
response bound is refused (`resource_exhausted`) rather than truncated: a
partial snapshot would make the cursor claim state the caller never read.

roles.description: The Project's Roles, in registration order.

roots.description: The Project's Roots, in registration order.

tasks.description: The Project's Tasks, in creation order.

ProviderRefusal.description:
Why the provider registration a dispatch profile names could not be
validated. Registry-owned facts only: credential material and verified
endpoint locality are execution-time Host concerns and never appear here.

oneOf.description:
No workforce binding resolved for the task's Role, so there is no
runtime profile to validate.
The profile names a connection the registry does not hold.
The profile names an entitlement the registry does not hold.
The profile names a model descriptor the registry does not hold.
The stored descriptor declares an unsupported provider contract version.
The stored descriptor's own token bounds are invalid.
Profile, connection, entitlement and model identities disagree.
The entitlement is expired at preparation time.
The authentication/billing combination is not supported.

candidates.description:
What this Host holds for each candidate the binding names, the primary
first and the fallbacks in the binding's own order — one entry per
candidate, so a report cannot silently omit one. The routing and
eligibility read this instead of inferring carriage from a runtime's
kind: for each candidate, the twelve surfaces, the demand the binding
itself makes, and what the declaration carries for every one of them.

max_cpu_millicores.description:
The CPU the candidate's dispatch needs, in millicores. Absent means the
candidate declares no CPU demand and the readiness report asks the Host
for none: concurrency is not a CPU reservation.

oneOf.description:
One pack's published Compatibility Dossier, served whole, and the run
inside it that this Host held against the runtime it actually has — named
by the upstream version and platform a reader looks that run up with. The
run is not copied out of the record: the dossier is served as published
and these two facts say which of its runs the Host held, so no reader has
to make the Host's comparison for itself.

The caller's authorized Project registry, in registration order. Each
entry is a canonical Project record, never a projection or a path. A
record-list response is a named field so the envelope stays an object
with its own `kind`.

host_paths.description: An observed placement, not identity or filesystem authorization.

oneOf.description: Derived entirely from recorded Team structure by an exact rule.
Closest partial coverage; recorded so heuristic routing stays auditable.

requested.description: Explicit assignment, preserved separately from the resolution.

resolved.description: None records a no-route diagnosis instead of a silent substitution.

oneOf.description: The explicitly requested Role is not a current Team member.
No executable non-lead Team member covers these domains.
An explicit Lead/user assignment, honored before any classification.
Every requested domain is covered by the resolved Role's task domains.
First partial domain coverage in deterministic Role order, not maximal coverage.

RuleRead.description:
One rule's outcome as a dossier publishes it: the rule's name, and whether
it held. The prose a rule holds is the suite's own and does not travel on
the wire — a reader learns the name and looks it up in the SDK that ran it,
so a reworded rule cannot make a published dossier read as a different rule.

id.description: The suite's name for this rule, exactly as a report carried it.

oneOf.description: Ready with no dependency edges at all.
Ready and every blocking dependency target is Completed.

SchedulableTask.description:
A scheduler query result: one Ready task whose blocking dependency targets
are all Completed and whose Change Stream is Active, with an explanation
of every constraint considered. Scheduling decisions must be explainable
from recorded state, so the reason is part of the record, not a log line.

SurfaceCarriage.description:
One surface of a binding's demand, with what the observed runtime declares
for each carrier. The entries and the delivery vocabulary are the contract
projection's own: what differs is which claims and capabilities are read,
not what a delivery means.

carried.description: One entry for every capability the binding's own facts require here.

preventive.description:
One entry for every control the binding declares a minimum for on this
surface, and none for a control it does not.

surface.description: The place this carriage is about.

oneOf.description: This task cannot start until the target completes.
This task consumes a versioned contract produced by the target.
This task blocks the target (stored on the blocking task).
This task independently reviews the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task independently verifies the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task supersedes the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task conflicts with the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.
This task follows up on the target. Recorded, not yet enforced.

fencing_token.description:
Monotonic per-task token: every acquisition increments it, and a
worker presenting an older token is fenced out of later mutations.

Timestamp.description: UTC milliseconds from Unix epoch, assigned by the authority, not a worker clock.

UnboundedLimit.description:
The declared limit a Host has no kernel bound for. A declared limit outside
the enforced set is a refusal, never a silent omission.

oneOf.description:
A CPU *rate* has no bound on Linux without cgroup delegation: RLIMIT_CPU
caps cumulative CPU time, not a rate, so the Host refuses rather than
substituting a different limit than the one declared.

VerificationEvidence.description:
A verifier-produced claim whose authenticity must be checked by the Host. This
value alone grants no authority. Each gate binds to a run, artifact, dispatch and
exact source/target pair; a runtime-local success flag is not evidence.

WorkerRun.description:
The outcome of one wired worker run. Completion evidence is journaled by
the store; this reports only what the caller can observe. A run whose
loop halted without a finished turn is an `Err` response (the task stays
Running; retry policy is the Host's), so `completed` is `true` in every
reachable `Ok` — it is the journaled-evidence marker, never a verified
completion.

completed.description:
Whether completion evidence was filed (task is now
CompletionRequested). Never implies verified completion.

runtime.description: The loop's runtime kind, echoed from the dispatch contract.

WorkforceRuntimeContract.description:
Historical dispatch contract. Fields have no setters: re-staffing produces a
new binding revision and a new Dispatch, never an in-place contract rewrite.

effective_access.description:
The least-privilege access this dispatch operates under: the binding's
authorized access narrowed to exactly this Task's Root. `None` only on
contracts journaled before narrowing existed (they fall back to the
full binding snapshot they were compiled with).

limits.description:
The resource limits this dispatch was staffed with. They are recorded,
not merely referenced: the Host binds the execution it produces to
exactly these, and a limit it cannot bind refuses that execution.
`None` only on contracts journaled before limits were recorded: they
deserialize rather than break replay, and activation refuses them for
having no bound to apply instead of running unbounded.

correlation_id.description: None only when parsing failed before a trusted correlation ID was decoded.

telemetry.description:
Lossy observations have no durable sequence and cannot be replayed as domain
events or treated as completion evidence. No arbitrary raw harness payloads.
telemetry.title: Telemetry
